newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Seoul shrs end lower as margin overhang hits mood.
newsitem.headline: Seoul shrs end lower as margin overhang hits mood.

text.p: Stocks closed lower on Wednesday for the eighth consecutive day as an overhang of loans for margin trading continued to depress sentiment, brokers said.
But they said a technical rebound was likely on Thursday as the composite stock index neared the 750 level.
Economic indicators showing a widening current account deficit and rising inventories also dampened buying sentiment.
"A technical rebound is likely tomorrow after the fall in the past week. But sentiment is running very weak," said Choo Hee-yup, a broker at Dongwon Securities.
The index ended 9.23 points lower to a provisional 757.09.
The central Bank of Korea reported on Wednesday the country's current account deficit soared to $1.41 billion in September from a $753.1 million shortfall a year earlier.
Inventories rose 20.4 percent in September, compared with a 11.3 percent rise a year before, according to the National Statistical Office.
Brokers said outstanding loans for margin trading totalled about three trillion won, while customer deposits at brokerage houses were at around 2.7 trillion.
They said between 200 and 900 billion won of loans would have to be paid back in November.
Brokers said a government plan to sell 13.3 million shares of Korea Telecom in November would be a depressing factor.

The finance ministry said after the close that it would sell 4.6 percent, or 500 billion won worth, of the state-backed telephone service provider. "The plan will worsen the already staggering stock market," said a Hyundai Securities broker.

A gloomy economic outlook will also weigh on the market for the time being. The state-funded Korea Development Institute said the country's GDP was expected to grow a real 6.8 percent this year, down from the government's earlier forecast of about seven percent. GDP grew nine percent in 1995.
